title: Stop Using Thread Tape on Flexible Supply Lines
description: Educational tip explaining why PTFE thread tape should not be applied to flexible hose connector nuts or compression fittings that rely on internal rubber washers.
image_prompt: A professional high-detail close-up cutaway section of a braided stainless steel faucet flexible supply hose nut threaded onto a brass shut-off valve outlet shank under a sink. The cutaway visual clearly shows the interior black rubber washer compressed flat against the smooth rim of the brass fitting to form the seal. The threads are clean, shiny metal-on-metal without any white PTFE thread tape. Photorealistic educational visual, macro focus on the brass threads and rubber washer interface, clean background under a sink with soft realistic lighting, vertical 9:16 aspect ratio composition, main subject centered, no text, no logos, no watermarks, no arrows, no labels, physically realistic plumbing components.
visual_story: The visual uses a clear educational cutaway to reveal how a flexible supply line actually seals water. Viewers will notice the internal rubber washer pressed against the flat top face of the brass pipe shank. This highlights that the seal happens at the rubber gasket interface, while the metal threads only exist to pull the gasket tight. Showing clean, tape-free threads helps the viewer visualize why adding thread tape is unnecessary and counterproductive for this connection type.

on_image_text.hook: Stop Wrapping Thread Tape on Flex Hose Nuts
on_image_text.explanation: Flexible supply lines seal using an internal rubber washer against a flat surface, not through the threads.
on_image_text.takeaway: Use tape only on tapered pipe threads (NPT). Keep flex line nuts clean and hand-tighten plus a quarter turn.
